title: Whole Numbers: Place Value, Ordering, Rounding and Estimating
seo_title: Grade 7 Whole Numbers Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Order, compare and represent whole numbers; recognise and use the place value of digits; round off and estimate; use the properties of whole numbers and calculation techniques including multiplying and dividing by powers of 10.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 whole numbers worksheets: place value, multiplying and dividing by powers of 10, ordering, rounding and estimating. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Compare from the left; round to estimate.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.
  • × 10 moves every digit one place to the left; ÷ 10 moves every digit one place to the right.
  • To compare, count the digits, then compare from the left. Use < and >.
  • Round off to estimate: 4 872 × 31 is about 5 000 × 30 = 150 000.

Examples

Example

Round 6 482 517 to the nearest 100 000

ten thousands digit 8

Answer: 6 500 000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Value or digit?The 4 in 6 482 517 is worth 400 000.
Comparing from the rightCompare from the left.
The wrong digitLook one place to the right.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: On a number line, −8,9 is to the right of −9,8, so −8,9 > −9,8. With negative numbers, the one further from zero is smaller.

items.q: 149 muffins are baked. A box holds 12 muffins. How many boxes can be filled completely?
